title: Constructible exceptional adjunction and domainwise coherence
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are separated of finite type. At $A_n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,A_n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category; at $R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$. Integral categories use completed coefficient sheaves and derived completeness with reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; field categories use rationalization and common finite coefficient-field stages, respectively. 

Let $f:X\to Y$ and choose any compactification $X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Such a compactification exists; $\overline X$ is of finite type over $k$ and has a nonnegative finite dimension bound $d$ (take $d=0$ if it is empty). Put $\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda$ and $D_T=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_T)$. On precisely $\mathcal C_{Y,\Lambda}$ the exceptional functor preserves the constructible domain and is canonically
$$Rf^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y,\qquad Rf_!\dashv Rf^!.$$
At finite coefficients this is the class-relative constructible adjunction for $c$, with its finite quotient cocycle, units and counits. At $R$ the pullback in the formula is completed and the adjunction is identified with its finite reductions; at $E$ it is the rationalized integral adjunction and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ the descended constructible adjunction. All units and counits are preserved by the stated coefficient comparisons. No unrestricted unbounded ambient right adjoint is required.
For the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum], all proved compactification, composition, exchange, projection, internal-Hom, orientation, exceptional and duality comparisons satisfy the identity, composition, exchange and projection equations on the intersections of their individual proved domains. Their coefficient comparisons preserve the defining evaluations and adjunction maps. Smooth orientation and site-perfect pairing retain exactly their additional proved purity and pairing compatibilities. At the field stages, for data and Weil objects descending to the finite field [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], these maps are Weil-equivariant. This conclusion asserts neither arbitrary-base-change commutation for Verdier duality nor a larger domain for any operation.

proof.text: For integral $L$, choose $[a,b]$ supporting $L_1$. Residue-Tor control gives this Tor interval for all reductions, since $\ell$ is invertible on $Y$. Apply the integral exceptional theorem to its specified coherent realization: $G_fL=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_n^!L_n$, right adjoint to integral compact support, equals $D_{X,R}f^*_{\mathrm{comp}}D_{Y,R}L$. Its output interval is $[a-2d_X,b+2d_Y]$; its reductions identify the unit and counit with the finite ones.

proof.text: The common-stage Verdier theorem supplies the $\Omega$-formula and constructible domains. Check the hypotheses of the common-field map-descent lemma: step 5 gives preservation of units, counits and evaluations under finite field extension; the closed-stage exceptional functor is defined through scalar comparisons coherent in successive field extensions; operation reduction makes compact support and tensor commute with common-stage scalar extension; the integral finite-extension comparisons of internal Hom and the dualizing object respect the identity extension, composition and tensor associators, and pass to the rationalized stages. Apply the lemma: its representative formulas give exactly the descended unit, counit, evaluation and triangle equations.

For finite-Tor internal Hom use the general finite Hom theorem; for integral Hom use its evaluation-transpose reduction; for finite field extension use the integral Hom and dualizing-object comparisons preserving evaluation and biduality. These give the asserted evaluation normalizations, without imposing site-perfectness on general finite-Tor or integral Hom.
